headline: Free checking this week, a Japan fund that grows every month, credit by summer
sproutSays: Your money comes in waves, and that's completely normal for a student. Let's give every dollar a job, starting with one free step you can take this week.

stepOne.title: Open FNB Student Checking this week
stepOne.detail: No monthly service charge and no minimum balance, so it costs nothing to start.

spendingPlan.note: Rent, phone, groceries, and the other bills that keep life running.
Grows your $800 cushion toward 3 months of costs ($1,950).
Coffee, movies, whatever you like. No guilt.

matches.explanation: Japan is your top goal, so it gets its own savings account. Keeping the trip money separate stops it from quietly getting spent.
termsToKnow: $50 minimum to open online ($0 in branch)
$5 monthly fee, waived with a $500 average daily balance
6 transfers or withdrawals a month; $15 for each one over

matches.explanation: Everything starts with a home base for your money. Student Checking has no monthly fee and no overdraft fees, and later it's where you'll pay your card from so you're never late.
termsToKnow: No monthly service charge or minimum balance
No overdraft fees; transactions are declined when funds are short
Refunds non-FNB ATM fees up to 4 times per statement cycle

matches.unlockCondition: When your savings reach $1,300, so the $500 deposit still leaves your $800 cushion
matches.explanation: A secured card is the most reliable way to start credit from a building range. We wait until the deposit won't eat your safety cushion.
termsToKnow: Credit limit equals your savings deposit, $500 to $2,000
APR not published; check current rate with FNB

matches.unlockCondition: When you start your full-time job
matches.explanation: Your place after graduation is years away, which suits a 12-month goal CD that renews. A steady paycheck makes the $25 monthly transfer easy.
termsToKnow: $100 minimum to open, plus at least $25 a month in transfers

notYet.reason: At $100 a month, Japan takes about 30 months, not 9. We're not cutting your cushion or guilt-free money to force it; extra income is the faster path.
notYet.revisitWhen: when your first paycheck or internship pay arrives

notYet.reason: A 12-month CD would lock your Japan money past your 9-month trip, and early withdrawal has a penalty.

bankerSummary: Maya, college student, no steady job, not yet an FNB customer. Income: $2,400 summer savings (one-time), $1,500 aid refund per semester, $200/mo from family = about $842/mo effective. Fixed costs $650, no debt, surplus $192/mo, savings $800, credit range: building. Goals: study abroad in Japan ($3,000 in 9 months, P1), build credit (12 months, P2), own a place after graduation (7 years, P3). Plan: Student Checking now, FirstRate Savings for Japan next, SmartSecured card at $1,300 savings, Savers Goal CD after a full-time job. Good fit for a student banking conversation.
disclaimer: Educational prototype. Not financial advice. No data is stored.
